verdict.rationale: Both changes replace repeated scans with a normalized-email index while preserving ordering, first-match behavior, and merging of incoming duplicates. B is preferable because it adds regression coverage for duplicate stored emails and reports passing tests and typechecking, whereas A adds no tests and was not verified. B's wall-clock performance assertion is a maintenance risk on slow or heavily loaded CI machines, but its additional coverage still gives it a slight advantage.
a_issues: Adds no regression tests for the optimization, particularly preservation of first-match behavior when existing contacts contain duplicate normalized emails.
Neither tests nor typechecking were run, and the performance improvement was not measured.
b_issues: The fixed one-second performance assertion is environment-dependent and may fail on slow or heavily loaded CI; a separate benchmark or deterministic complexity regression check would be more robust.
